title: Pure Component Render Inspector
subtopicTitle: Render Phase vs Commit Phase Mechanics
concept: Idempotence and Purity in Component Body
problemStatement: Implement `verifyRenderPurity(componentFn, props)` that runs `componentFn(props)` twice consecutively. If the output varies or side-effect counters change between runs, returns `{ isPure: false }`, otherwise `{ isPure: true, output }`.
interviewTrap: React StrictMode renders components TWICE in development specifically to uncover impure renders and accidental side effects.

testCases.name: Identifies pure deterministic render
testCases.testFn: const PureComp = p => ({ tag: 'h1', text: p.name }); return verifyRenderPurity(PureComp, { name: 'Alice' }).isPure;

testCases.name: Flags impure component mutating external counter
testCases.testFn: let globalCount = 0; const ImpureComp = () => ({ val: ++globalCount }); return verifyRenderPurity(ImpureComp, {}).isPure;

details.name: Flags impure component mutating external counter

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: React's pipeline is divided into two distinct phases: The **Render Phase** (pure computation, diffing, finding changes) and the **Commit Phase** (applying changes to the host DOM and executing side-effects). A Pure Component Render Inspector checks whether component functions remain pure and side-effect free during the render phase.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Accept a component render function and props.
Instrument global environment to intercept side-effects (e.g. DOM mutations, global variable writes).
Invoke the component render function twice (simulating React's `<StrictMode>` double-render in development).
Compare the two outputs: both renders must return identical element trees without mutating external state.
Report any detected impurities or differences.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Concurrent Mode, the Render Phase can be paused, aborted, restarted, or thrown away if higher-priority work arrives. If a component performs side-effects (e.g. `window.count++`) during render, those side-effects execute unpredictably multiple times.

complexity.time: O(R) where R is the render execution time of the component.

edgeCasesHandled: Pure functions pass with zero flagged side-effects.
Impure side-effects during render (mutating external state) are detected.

specifications: React Official Docs: Keeping Components Pure
React Source: ReactStrictMode.js (Double-invoking component renders in dev)
verifiedRules: Render phase must be pure and free of observable side effects.
Side effects must be deferred strictly to the commit phase (useEffect / useLayoutEffect).

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is the difference between the Render Phase and Commit Phase in React?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: 1) **Render Phase**: Pure computation. React calls component functions, calculates Virtual DOM diffs, and computes effect flags. It is side-effect-free, asynchronous, and interruptible (can be paused, restarted, or aborted in Concurrent Mode). 2) **Commit Phase**: DOM mutation and side effects. React synchronously applies calculated mutations to the host DOM (`commitMutationEffects`), runs synchronous layout effects (`useLayoutEffect`), and schedules passive effects (`useEffect`). It is synchronous and un-interruptible.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Core architectural lifecycle distinction in modern React.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why does React StrictMode invoke component render functions twice in development?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `<StrictMode>` intentionally double-invokes component bodies, `useState` initializers, and `useMemo` callbacks in development to detect unintended side-effects (e.g. mutating global variables, modifying props). Pure functions produce identical outputs on repeated calls; impure functions reveal bugs immediately under double rendering.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of React's purity requirements and developer tooling.

realWorldUseCases.description: Detecting developers accidentally calling `setState` directly inside the render body instead of inside `useEffect`.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: function Bad() { setCount(c => c + 1); return null; } // Error: Maximum update depth exceeded

howToExplain.opening: React separates rendering into an interruptible, side-effect-free Render Phase and a synchronous, atomic Commit Phase.
keyPoints: Render phase calculates diffs and must be 100% pure (idempotent).
Commit phase applies mutations to the real DOM synchronously.
StrictMode double-renders in development to expose impure side-effects.
Side effects must strictly live in useEffect, useLayoutEffect, or event handlers.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Keeping the render phase pure is the prerequisite for React Concurrent Mode and server-side rendering to function correctly.
analogies: Drafting an email: typing and revising drafts (render) can happen multiple times without anyone seeing; clicking 'Send' (commit) is the irreversible real-world action.

commonMistakes.mistake: Mutating window or global variables directly inside the component body.
commonMistakes.why: In Concurrent Mode, renders can be aborted and restarted; global mutations will execute unpredictably multiple times.
commonMistakes.correct: Move all observable side effects into useEffect or event handlers.

followUpDeepDive.question: Which component lifecycles / hooks belong to the Render Phase?
followUpDeepDive.answer: Component body execution, `useState` initializers, `useReducer` reducer functions, `useMemo`, and class `render()` and `shouldComponentUpdate()` belong to the Render Phase.
